stem:
The diagram shows a small letter viewed through three pieces of glass held close to the page: a convex lens (P), a concave lens (Q), and a flat transparent glass piece (R).

How does the letter appear in each case?

options.text: Through P the letter looks erect and enlarged; through Q it looks erect and smaller; through R it looks the same size and shape.
Through P, Q, and R the letter looks erect and enlarged.
Through P the letter looks smaller; through Q it looks enlarged; through R it looks inverted.
Through R the letter looks enlarged, because any clear glass enlarges the letter.

teacher.key_rationale: Close to the page, a convex lens magnifies erect, a concave lens makes a diminished erect image, and flat glass does not change size. Saying all three enlarge over-widens the rule. Swapping which lens enlarges drops the lens-type condition. Judging from clear glass alone is a surface cue.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote plane-mirror ray figure into three close-up viewing panels for convex lens, concave lens, and flat glass.
